trigger: a cold validation captured the cache epoch, a targeted local erase (sign-out, deactivation, reactivation, password change) ran, then the validation inserts its pre-erase session
summary: Targeted erases did not bump session_cache_epoch_. Five reviewers independently found no interleaving that survives past the next generation poll (about 1 s, 30 s under poll failure) because every durable mutation bumps the generation; impact class disputed (I1 vs I8), orchestrator and reviewers settled I8 as the poll is the specified bound. Remedy chosen by Dave: bump at every targeted erase. Fix: 13895c9746 bumps the epoch at every targeted erase via drop_cached_*_locked; T-R9 pins it.
classification_rationale: the 'local erase is immediate' reading was not true of the code; the bound is the generation poll

trigger: an idle-expired cache hit re-reads the store row (from_store=true) and re-caches the session without the account gate
summary: The step-4 idle re-read was the only store-built session published into sessions_ without the account gate, so 'store-built sessions are gated' was not literally true. Bounded by the generation poll. Also raised by: authdb, cpp-expert, security-guardian. Fix: f3b63fbd40: one gate call after the idle re-read and before the cache insert; T-R3 gate form.
classification_rationale: gate comment and docs asserted every store-built session is gated

trigger: a future persisted auth_source other than local/oidc/saml, or a hand-edited stored engine_token row, would not be gated by the allow-list
summary: Gate scope was `auth_source == local` only. Dave ruled the closed three-way (local gated, oidc/saml pass, anything else refused + counted). Also raised by: architect. Fix: f3b63fbd40: session_account_admits closed three-way, yuzu_auth_session_unknown_source_total; 1ba7afd8c0 rewrites the one test whose premise changed.
classification_rationale: plan text said neither oidc nor saml; code was a plain allow-list

trigger: a login whose first factor verified before a deactivation mints after the reactivation (post-mint recheck compares role, credential hash, active state only)
summary: Docs and a code comment said a sign-in completing after a reactivation is a new sign-in; the pre-existing residual is not that strong. Also raised by: unhappy-path, compliance-officer. Fix: docs c581bae77d,93d42f6d7e; code comment in the polish commit d2e47bab1b.
classification_rationale: doc sentence overstates; residual pre-dates this change

adjudicated_by: Dave Rae (the change's owner, not the author of this run's commits: they were written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 agents), non-author adjudicator via the questions window 2026-11-13
adjudication_rationale: Facts restated from the HIGH (I5(b)) derivation to I5/E5: bounded by lock_timeout per wait and not persistent, so no raise; accepted trade-off R4 recorded in plan v2 and approved by Dave; sre and compliance-officer independently derived MEDIUM.
trigger: a stuck or queued session_meta writer: the deactivation transaction's last statement (the session-generation bump) cannot lock the row within lock_timeout
summary: Unhappy-path derived HIGH (I5(b)); compliance-officer and sre derived MEDIUM (bounded, loud, retry-safe, and every deprovision path already writes session_meta via invalidate_user first). Dave adjudicated MEDIUM, accepted (plan R4), document only. The lock-wait bound is per wait (2000 ms, up to five waits, about 10 s, plus up to 4 s pool acquire), not 'about 2 s'. Also raised by: chaos-injector. Fix: documented: docs 3a2357bb52,93d42f6d7e; owner comments a6b42cc517); no code change by rulin.
classification_rationale: availability trade-off of failing closed; the '~2 s' wording understated it

trigger: read_generation routed to a lagging standby or pooled read replica stamps last-success on stale data
summary: Stale-serve bound unbounded if generation reads are served by a lagging standby. Not introduced here; deployment contract is a single primary.

trigger: a login wave bumps the generation, every replica clears its cache at most once per second and each cold local read costs two queries and two pool leases from the shared pool
summary: Cold-read doubling; worst tail about 2.0 s to about 3.5 s; pool exhaustion now gives 401. Reasoned, not measured (chaos CH-2 designed, not run). Also raised by: performance.

trigger: replay of a valid-but-inactive cookie costs find plus user_exists per request, uncached
summary: Replay of a deactivated account's cookie (needs a valid token) costs two queries per request until the row expires; no self-heal by design (plan D4). Also raised by: performance.
classification_rationale: bounded cost, same class as the existing random-cookie find

trigger: COMMIT acknowledgement lost on deactivation: caller sees 503, account is inactive and bumped, the retry meets 404 and the SCIM mirror stays active
